text.p: - Slovenia agreed to the construction of Russia's Gazprom gas network that would run through Slovenia to Italy with a length of 318 km (194 miles).
- Parliament is expected to discuss the government's proposal on freezing salaries of parliamentary members and other state top officials on Wednesday.

- Economists welcomed the government's proposal to freeze the highest salaries as a start to the country's overall savings initiative. Average monthly net salary of 90 parliamentary members in February was 360,753 tolars ($2,344).

- A two-day working meeting of NATO and partner countries ended in Brdo, Slovenia on Tuesday. Participants discussed NATO's enlargement but did not talk about the possible first countries that would join the alliance.
- Slovenia's airline Adria Airways resumed flights to Tirana after a two-week halt. Adria will fly to Tirana from Ljubljana four times a week.
- Slovenia's unemployment in February rose to 125,534, a 1.5 increase from the same month in 1996, the country's unemployment office said.
- Priorities of Slovenian foreign policy remain unchanged -- joining EU and NATO, relations with neighbouring countries, U.S. and Russia, said Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler.
- Slovenia's largest bank Nova Ljubljanska Banka will give a $400,000 loan to Russian Telecom for buying telephone equipment from Slovenian producer Iskratel.
- Between 1996 and 2000, Slovenian Telekom plans to invest 90 billion tolars ($584.8 million), mainly in the modernisation of its network.
